summary: Worker thread that owns the EmbeddingGemma session for the embedder daemon: loads embed-runtime with workerData {dir, threads}, posts 'ready', then answers {id, texts, role} with transferred Float32Array vectors or an error. Exists because session.run blocks the thread it runs on; the daemon can terminate() it to break a stuck inference.

summary: One model PROCESS for the embedder daemon (forked with an IPC channel, serialization 'advanced'), used for both MAIN and the query lane; args are a JSON {dir, threads} in argv[2]. Ops, run strictly one at a time: embed {texts, role} → Float32Array[], plan {text, role} → {tokens, windows} (the daemon's lane-start rule reads tokens), windows, sums {ids} → unnormalised Float64Array; every reply carries the process RSS. It exits on IPC 'disconnect', so a kill -9 of the daemon leaves no orphan (it exits after any run in progress). It is no longer a worker_thread: a pre-4b daemon that still has this file loaded as a thread would fail a watchdog restart.

summary: One model PROCESS for the embedder daemon (forked with an IPC channel, serialization 'advanced'), used for both MAIN and the query lane; it holds an ONNX session and NO tokenizer (the daemon tokenizes and sends ids). argv[2] is JSON {dir, threads, protocol}: when protocol ≠ PROTOCOL it exits 3 — an OLD daemon still running after an update that forks this new file gets a failed spawn instead of a process speaking a different IPC (measured: a protocol-1 daemon starting against new files → 'main model process exited (3)' → model unavailable, no orphan). Ops, run strictly one at a time: embed {plans} → unit Float32Array[] (via embedPlanned, windowed plans pooled here — queries are one call each); sums {rows} → Float64Array[] (one padded run; the daemon's per-window backfill). Every reply carries the process RSS. Exits on IPC 'disconnect', so a kill -9 of the daemon leaves no orphan. A process, not a worker_thread: worker.terminate() during an in-flight ORT run ABORTS the whole process (libc++abi Napi::Error, 3/3 on M1 Pro 2026-11-22), so a watchdog could not kill a stuck thread.
